title: Q versus K: 2 and 3
hook: Compare a mixture with its equilibrium ratio.

knows: Reversible reactions have forward and reverse processes.
doesNotKnow: How the initial reaction quotient predicts net direction.

misconception: At equilibrium all molecular reactions stop.
objective: Compare Q and K to predict initial net direction.

claims.text: For the ideal model A ⇌ B, K = 3, initial [A] = 2 mol/L, and initial [B] = 4 mol/L. What is the initial net direction? Q = [B]/[A] = 4/2 = 2. Q is less than K, so the net reaction initially proceeds toward B.
A and B represent an ideal hypothetical 1:1 interconversion at fixed temperature.
Recall: What does Q = K indicate for a reversible reaction at fixed conditions? At equilibrium forward and reverse rates are equal, so there is no net change.
As the ideal mixture changes, its reaction quotient moves toward the equilibrium value at the stated temperature.

recall.question: What does Q = K indicate for a reversible reaction at fixed conditions?
options: Reaction has stopped in both directions
recall.why: At equilibrium forward and reverse rates are equal, so there is no net change.
